summary: Saves a named snapshot of a store and restores it later — a checkpoint, rather than the moving history State History keeps.
description: Save captures the store as it is now; Restore writes it back as a single commit that subscribers see as an ordinary change. A snapshot is copied in on restore, so **the same snapshot can be restored any number of times** — which is what makes it usable as a reset point rather than a one-shot. `snapshot` outputs the captured value, and `snapshotData` accepts one back, so a snapshot can be round-tripped through JSON: persisted, sent to a server, or restored in another session. As with State History, values that could only be captured by reference are not deep-copied, and `fullyRestorable` / `byReferenceKeys` name them rather than letting the checkpoint quietly under-deliver. Errors are reported on the Error output instead of thrown out of a signal handler.
whenToUse: A discrete checkpoint: 'reset this form', 'revert to the last saved version', 'restore the state I shipped this bug report with'. Use State History instead when you want undo/redo over every change; use this when you want one or two named points you return to deliberately. The `snapshot`/`snapshotData` pair is also the straightforward way to persist state across sessions or attach it to a bug report.

ports.storeName: The store to capture or restore.
ports.snapshotName: A label for the snapshot, so several checkpoints are distinguishable in a UI.
ports.snapshotData: A snapshot captured earlier, fed back in to be restored — the input side of the round trip through JSON.
ports.restore: Writes a snapshot back as one commit. Safe to fire repeatedly; the snapshot is copied in, not consumed.
ports.snapshot: The captured snapshot, for persisting, transmitting, or feeding into another Restore.
ports.fullyRestorable: Whether this snapshot can be fully restored, or holds values captured only by reference.
ports.done: Fires after a Save or a Restore you triggered succeeded, whichever it was — wire this when one chain follows both verbs.
ports.error: Carries a refused save or restore — an unknown store, or snapshot data that could not be read.

patterns: Save when a form opens, Restore on the Cancel button — a reset that needs no knowledge of the form's fields.
`snapshot` → JSON → persisted, then back through `snapshotData` on the next load, for state that survives a reload without a live store.
Attach a snapshot to a bug report so the state is reproducible rather than described.
antiPatterns: Using it for undo. It is a checkpoint, not a stack — State History keeps the ordered history.
Assuming a restore is total when `fullyRestorable` is false: keys in `byReferenceKeys` share their object with the snapshot.
Saving on every change. That is a history with extra steps, and unbounded — State History bounds itself.
